clue.text: Sweet, small beer

definitions.meaning: a sweet is a British dessert course, and this layered pudding of sponge, custard and cream is one
small beer is something of little importance, a trivial matter

explanation.surface: A puzzling list: a sweet thing and a weak beer, as if ordering at a pub.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a British layered dessert, and a thing of no consequence, which is what small beer means.

clue.text: Silent act I developed with short performance

indicators.note: something developed has been worked into a new form, so the letters of act I are rearranged

parts.note: a turn is a brief act in a variety show

explanation.surface: An actor's first act grew into a wordless piece alongside a brief sketch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'developed' signals the anagram; 'act' tempts as the performance, but the performance is the music-hall turn.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone reserved who says little is described this way; it is a near synonym of silent.

clue.text: Relative collected by two individuals, friend not moving

indicators.note: the relative is gathered up between the two individuals, so it sits inside them

parts.note: I is a single one, so two of them give I and I
nan is an informal word for a grandmother
mate is British slang for a friend

explanation.surface: Granny is picked up by two people, while a pal sits motionless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'collected by' puts NAN between the two I's.
explanation.definitionFit: Lifeless or motionless things are without movement; the adjective means showing no sign of life.

clue.text: Those drawn in great quantity

definitions.meaning: in a draw or ballot, slips are drawn to decide something, as in drawing straws
an informal adverb for a great deal

explanation.surface: Raffle tickets pulled out in large numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: Lots are what one draws to decide by chance, and lots also means a great deal informally.

clue.text: English county Republican place, little bit to the left

indicators.note: in an across answer, what is to the left comes first, so the little bit goes before the rest

parts.note: some means a small amount, as in 'have some'
to set something is to place it

explanation.surface: A political note: a Republican seat in England, edged slightly leftwards.
explanation.walkthrough: SOMERSET is a county in South West England.
explanation.definitionFit: This is one of the shire counties of England, in the West Country, so it is an example of the definition.

clue.text: Occasionally relating to cooler teacher

parts.note: of means concerning, as in 'tales of woe'
a fan cools the air
a don is a university lecturer

explanation.surface: Something now and then concerns a teacher who keeps cool.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means intermittently, now and again, which is a synonym of occasionally.

clue.text: All inside bandage, very thin gauze

indicators.note: the letters sit inside the run of words bandage, very thin gauze, spanning their breaks

explanation.surface: Everything is wrapped inside a bandage of very fine gauze.
explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun means the whole lot, every thing there is, which is what all means.

clue.text: Capital up until now cut, one's assumed

indicators.note: to assume is to take on or take in, so one is taken into the shortened phrase
cut means the last letter is lopped off the phrase

parts.note: so far means up to this point
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A city budget has been trimmed so far, with one figure taken as given.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' trims SO FAR to SOFA; 'assumed' takes I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sofia is the capital city of Bulgaria, so it is an example of a capital.

clue.text: Spanish city shepherded in as well

indicators.note: in places the guided word inside the word for also

parts.note: too means also, as well
to shepherd is to guide or lead, so shepherded means led

explanation.surface: A flock was guided into a city in Spain as well.
explanation.definitionFit: Toledo is a historic city in central Spain, so it is an example of the definition.

clue.text: Move round first of rooms in private area

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the verb for move goes around the letter

parts.note: to go is to move

indicators.note: first of picks the opening letter of rooms

explanation.surface: An estate agent's note: move round the first of the rooms into a private space.
explanation.definitionFit: A euphemism: the area where the thigh meets the abdomen is a private part of the body.

clue.text: Might schooner be supported by this vessel?

definitions.text: Might schooner be supported by this
definitions.meaning: a schooner is also a tall beer or sherry glass, and a small mat put under a glass protects the table
a ship that sails along a coast from port to port

explanation.surface: A sailing question: is a schooner held up by another boat?
explanation.walkthrough: 'schooner' looks like the sailing ship; here it is the large drinking glass.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a drinks mat for a glass, and a ship that trades along the shore.

clue.text: Worried, patching up fur with felt

indicators.note: patching up means mending by reworking materials, so the letters of fur and felt are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone anxious is repairing a fur coat with a felt patch.
explanation.definitionFit: Being anxious and uneasy is to be in a state of worry, so the adjective is a synonym.

clue.text: Grasp piece of wood

definitions.meaning: informal British for understand, as in 'I finally got it'
a small thin branch of a tree

explanation.surface: Take hold of a bit of timber.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: to catch on or understand, and a slender shoot or branch.

clue.text: Send lady in to design theme park

indicators.note: to design is to plan a new arrangement, so the letters of send lady in are reworked

explanation.surface: A boss sends a woman in to lay out an amusement park.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the famous Californian amusement resort built around cartoon characters, an example of a theme park.

clue.text: Yak sitting on male toad

indicators.note: in a down answer, what sits on something comes above it, so the chatter goes first

explanation.walkthrough: 'Yak' looks like the ox; it is the verb for chattering.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a European species of toad with a yellow stripe down its back, an example of the definition.

clue.text: On with old commander, new president

explanation.definitionFit: Ronald Reagan was the fortieth President of the United States, an example of a president.

clue.text: Progressive authorisation

definitions.meaning: an adjective for enterprising and forward-looking, as in 'a forward-looking firm'
permission to proceed, a green light

explanation.surface: Permission granted for forward-thinking plans.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: as an adjective, enterprising and modern; as a noun, approval to start.

clue.text: African people in a Salinger novel

indicators.note: novel means new or fresh, so the letters of a Salinger take a new order

explanation.surface: North Africans appear as characters in a book by J. D. Salinger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book by Salinger; it is the adjective meaning new.
explanation.definitionFit: Citizens of Algeria in North Africa, so they are an example of an African people.

clue.text: Member perhaps with good reason to worry about mark on ballot paper

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the scrambled letters go round the ballot mark
to worry something is to work at it and disturb it, so the letters of good and reason are tossed about

parts.note: voters put a cross, X, beside their choice

explanation.surface: A party member has good cause to fret over a cross on the ballot paper.

explanation.definitionFit: A euphemism: member is an old polite word for the penis, hence 'perhaps', an example of the category.

clue.text: That's too much to say: end broadcast

explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' looks like radio or TV; it means scattered.
explanation.definitionFit: An exclamation urging restraint, said when someone goes too far, so it means an interjection like 'enough'.

clue.text: Deterioration around the elements, say?

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the word for deterioration goes around the

parts.note: wear is damage from use, as in wear and tear

explanation.definitionFit: Rain, wind and sun are often called the elements, so the conditions outdoors are an example of them.

clue.text: Last seen of dark, dark piece

parts.note: dark as a noun means the time without light, night-time

explanation.definitionFit: In chess this is one of the pieces, moving in an L-shape, so it is an example of a piece.

clue.text: Items identified here with introduction of scholar's essays

parts.note: these is the pronoun for things pointed out close by

indicators.note: the introduction of a word is its opening letter, here the start of scholar's

explanation.surface: These pieces, with a scholar's foreword, are presented as academic essays.
explanation.definitionFit: Dissertations written for a degree are long essays, so the plural noun is a synonym of the definition.

clue.text: Just one side

definitions.meaning: the opposite of left, one of two sides

explanation.surface: Merely a single side.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: what is morally fair, and the direction opposite to left.

clue.text: Penned by Bach, is trio nicely dramatic?

explanation.walkthrough: 'Penned by' looks like 'written by'; it means enclosed.
explanation.definitionFit: Theatrical and over-emotional behaviour is called this; the word comes from the Latin for an actor.

clue.text: Fine cut, by the sound of it?

indicators.note: the clue tells us the word for cut is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: to shear is to cut, as wool from sheep

explanation.surface: A tailor judges a delicate trim purely by its sound.
explanation.definitionFit: A very thin, delicate fabric such as fine stockings is described with this adjective.

clue.text: Giant a tailless bird knocked over

indicators.note: knocked over means upended, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: a crow is a black bird

explanation.surface: A giant bird with no tail is bowled over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knocked over' turns A plus CRO into ORCA.
explanation.definitionFit: The killer whale is a huge marine mammal, so it is an example of a giant.

clue.text: Sheet of ice in continuous stream, we hear?

indicators.note: we hear means the word for stream is to be taken by its sound

parts.note: a flow is a steady continuous stream

explanation.surface: A slab of ice drifting in a steady current.
explanation.definitionFit: A floating flat mass of sea ice is the meaning, a sheet of ice.

clue.text: Situation where report written after book

indicators.note: written after means the second piece follows the first

parts.note: She is a novel by H. Rider Haggard

explanation.walkthrough: SHE is a famous adventure novel by H. Rider Haggard.

clue.text: Mountainous around a mountaineer ultimately — like him?

definitions.text: Mountainous around a mountaineer ultimately — like him?

indicators.note: around means surrounding, so the hilly word goes round the rest

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of mountaineer

explanation.walkthrough: Sir Edmund Hillary, the New Zealand climber, made the first ascent of Everest; the whole clue points to him.

clue.text: Batting — when out?

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the batter facing the bowler is 'the striker'.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: hitting the ball in cricket, and taking part in a walk-out by workers.

clue.text: Fewer appointments. one's learned

parts.note: less means a smaller amount, fewer
